entries.title: Test 2 odor assay layout and within-stage drift correction
entries.text: ### What was measured Test 2 contains **72 observed wells**: six stimulus rows × twelve construct positions. Its archive key is `odor-2026-10-21`; the source exports record 21 October 2026 with no timezone. It is distinct from Test 1, the four-acquisition assay, and its column order must not be transferred from that assay. Rows B/C were not supplied here; they are not gain-based exclusions from this dataset. ![Odor panel: construct mapping and recorded acquisition windows](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/3539a705f9f880fdad4b41ae2d8323c585a7eeb27b7dd26d218b5cf3809f08bc.avif) *An experimental schematic based on the supplied map and exported sampling times. It describes the observed assay layout and calculation, not a measured molecular mechanism.* | Row | Addition | Supplied preparation | |---|---|---| | A | VUAA1 | 1:100 dilution | | D | Isopentyl acetate | 1:1,000 dilution | | E | 2-Heptanone | 1:1,000 dilution | | F | Valeric acid | 1:1,000 dilution | | G | Pentyl acetate | 1:1,000 dilution | | H | DMSO vehicle | 0.1% DMSO | The user reports 0.1% DMSO for the solutions. These preparation facts are retained as supplied; absolute molar concentrations cannot be inferred from dilution factors alone. The older assay's nominal VUAA1 concentration is not reused here. | Column | Condition | Corresponding composite | |---|---|---| | 1 | Or7a+ORCO | [BBa_26ZAGFK0](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26zagfk0#odor-2026-10-21) | | 2 | Or19a+ORCO | [BBa_2629NIWH](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-2629niwh#odor-2026-10-21) | | 3 | Or22a+ORCO | [BBa_26WOX4B1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26wox4b1#odor-2026-10-21) | | 4 | Or35a+ORCO | [BBa_26LLF3LM](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26llf3lm#odor-2026-10-21) | | 5 | Or42a+ORCO | [BBa_26Q1Q094](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26q1q094#odor-2026-10-21) | | 6 | Or59b+ORCO | [BBa_26Y7CI2H](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26y7ci2h#odor-2026-10-21) | | 7 | Or67a+ORCO | [BBa_265G8CE1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-265g8ce1#odor-2026-10-21) | | 8 | Or67b+ORCO | [BBa_269VSDDR](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-269vsddr#odor-2026-10-21) | | 9 | Or85b+ORCO | [BBa_26K1TU11](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26k1tu11#odor-2026-10-21) | | 10 | Or98a+ORCO | [BBa_26TZLBMJ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26tzlbmj#odor-2026-10-21) | | 11 | ORCO only | [BBa_26E11Z80](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80#odor-2026-10-21) | | 12 | No transfection | Cellular background control; no part assigned | ### Primary calculation: change within F1 minus change within F0 For each well, use the first and last actual reading in each acquisition: - **ΔF0 = 100 × [F0(48 s) / F0(0 s) − 1]**, in percent. - **ΔF1 = 100 × [F1(168 s) / F1(0 s) − 1]**, in percent. - **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). F0 has five readings at 12 s intervals and F1 has fifteen. This subtracts the observed baseline-stage disturbance from the observed within-F1 fluorescence change. It uses separate denominators for the two stages. No baseline line is extrapolated to 168 s, and no rate, peak value or mean F1/F0 ratio is substituted for these endpoints. The primary S windows are unequal: **48 s of F0 versus 168 s of F1**. Therefore the data also include **S48 = 100 × [F1(48 s)/F1(0 s) − 1] − ΔF0**, using equal 48 s windows. S48 is a sensitivity view of the recorded data, not an independent replicate or evidence that the longer-duration result is incorrect. The separate vehicle contrast is **S(stimulus,c) − S(H,c)**. A further no-transfection contrast subtracts the corresponding vehicle contrast in column 12. These are differences between individual wells, with shared references; they remain dependent descriptive comparisons. Vehicle subtraction is additional to the primary within-well drift subtraction. ### Relation to Test 1 Test 1 had four acquisitions: a baseline before the blank addition, the blank round, a baseline before the test addition and the test round. Its retained calculation uses peak-three fluorescence changes and subtracts the blank-round excursion. Test 2 has only F0 and F1. **S is not the Test 1 R metric**, and these results are not pooled as replicated measurements of a single statistic. The Test 1 values remain unchanged and separately defined in their original tables. The mean-ratio metric **100 × (mean F1 / mean F0 − 1)** remains in the [mean-ratio audit](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv). It describes a different question and no longer supplies the main response conclusion. An F1 trajectory can rise even if its entire acquisition lies below the earlier F0 acquisition. Source timestamps do not identify the injection time, so no continuous injection-aligned trace is inferred. ### Reproducible inputs and limits There is one observed well per condition–addition pair. Five baseline readings and fifteen subsequent readings are within-well sampling, not twenty biological replicates. Numeric acquisition settings, stock molarities, addition-to-read delay and clone/culture lineage are not independently established from these exports. Within-stage normalization avoids making the between-acquisition level offset the response metric; it does not establish the biological cause of the trajectory. Local attachments: [corrected summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [mean-ratio audit](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv), [analysis metadata](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/05775ad28370-change-summary.json) and [import manifest](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json). Original measurements remain under `zenodo-release/aerosense-wiki/data/odor-2026-10-21/raw/`. New files have not been assigned an invented public DOI or Registry URL.

entries.title: Test 2 complete odor panel after baseline-stage disturbance subtraction
entries.text: ### Full-panel response and controls ![All measured conditions: within-F1 change minus within-F0 drift](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/3acf14605b324b4b7c5f2e70b5305898aa375a5ddcaaa079c1f96ca3990602e6.avif) *Each displayed value is S in percentage points from one observed well. The baseline and subsequent windows are 48 s and 168 s. The same definition is applied to every condition; the accompanying S48 column in the data attachment retains the equal-duration sensitivity calculation.* Across the twelve VUAA1 conditions, **11/12 S values are positive**, ranging from **-0.11 to +39.23 pp**. The ORCO-only condition gives **+18.69 pp** and the no-transfection condition gives **-0.11 pp**. These directions refer to baseline-drift-adjusted trajectories, not a percentage of validated receptors or independent success rate. The raw F1 first-to-last change is positive in **10/12 VUAA1 wells**. In the remaining conditions, a positive S can arise from a smaller decrease in F1 than in F0. The table keeps both stage changes visible so that this distinction is inspectable. | Column | Condition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | VUAA1 S (pp) | DMSO S (pp) | VUAA1 − DMSO (pp) | VUAA1 S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | Or7a + ORCO | -1.87 | -1.47 | +0.40 | -1.79 | +2.19 | +1.13 | | 2 | Or19a + ORCO | -2.27 | +6.67 | +8.94 | -0.49 | +9.43 | +6.13 | | 3 | Or22a + ORCO | -2.31 | +11.13 | +13.44 | -1.66 | +15.10 | +9.25 | | 4 | Or35a + ORCO | -2.57 | +34.09 | +36.67 | -1.39 | +38.06 | +19.67 | | 5 | Or42a + ORCO | -2.57 | +36.66 | +39.23 | -0.31 | +39.54 | +23.53 | | 6 | Or59b + ORCO | -1.71 | +15.71 | +17.42 | -1.29 | +18.71 | +12.19 | | 7 | Or67a + ORCO | -2.49 | +18.93 | +21.42 | -1.08 | +22.50 | +9.11 | | 8 | Or67b + ORCO | -2.29 | +11.09 | +13.39 | -0.81 | +14.20 | +3.72 | | 9 | Or85b + ORCO | -1.08 | +16.44 | +17.52 | -1.47 | +18.99 | +13.84 | | 10 | Or98a + ORCO | -2.68 | +26.78 | +29.46 | -1.37 | +30.83 | +9.82 | | 11 | ORCO only | -1.13 | +17.56 | +18.69 | -0.92 | +19.61 | +8.85 | | 12 | No transfect | -2.85 | -2.96 | -0.11 | -1.20 | +1.08 | -7.83 | ![Same-construct vehicle differences of the corrected endpoint contrast](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/27397eb2b82b3fa8ef407088853b2be9ae79d0f8cbe7e6da5abb872351910328.avif) *This panel compares S in a stimulus well with S in a separate DMSO well of the same construct. The shared H reference makes comparisons dependent. It does not replace the primary within-well correction or prove tuning-receptor specificity.* The [complete within-stage trace atlas](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/005c7c6a370d-current-change-traces.svg) and [additional no-transfection contrast](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/6c5922212a32-current-double-difference.svg) make the observed trajectories and reference dependence inspectable. Each composite page has its complete six-addition plot and table. No-transfection and ORCO-only controls are cellular controls, not cell-free measurements. ![No-transfection condition, with within-stage normalization and drift subtraction](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/75b437f7b7eba8f1d6a7561860a05a81114102ce0c37ad761e3d7decebdc13a7.avif) *Column 12 uses the same calculation as the engineered conditions. Its result is not attributed to the reporter or tuning-receptor construct.* ### Exploratory supplement: VUAA1-referenced odor responses For each Test 2 construct, this supplementary ratio compares its odorant response with its own VUAA1 reference, using the same disturbance-corrected S values defined above: **N(odor, construct) = [S(odor, construct) − S(DMSO, construct)] / [S(VUAA1, construct) − S(DMSO, construct)].** N is dimensionless. DMSO maps to 0 and VUAA1 to 1 by construction; these are reference anchors, **not biological lower and upper bounds**. Negative values are retained, and values above 1 would also be retained. No clipping, absolute-value denominator or min–max transformation is applied. This supplement does not replace the original S or S48 values. ![Test 2 odor responses relative to each construct's VUAA1 and DMSO references](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/59c23fd55f95894cabb6daa1abd8f5c3edc69c9188045b462d2e2301761f8c52.avif) *Or7a–Or98a coexpress ORCO; ORCO only is the reporter-fusion control. Each row uses its own positive VUAA1-minus-DMSO denominator. Orange cells retain negative ratios. The dagger marks Or7a's small +2.19 pp reference, which makes its ratios sensitive to that denominator. VUAA1 = 1 and DMSO = 0 are calculation anchors. Each odorant, VUAA1 and DMSO condition has one observed well; four odorant ratios share the same two reference wells and are dependent comparisons, not replicated estimates. The no-transfection control remains in the S analyses above and is not used as a VUAA1-normalized receptor condition.* | Condition | VUAA1 − DMSO reference (pp) | Isopentyl acetate N | 2-Heptanone N | Valeric acid N | Pentyl acetate N | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Or7a + ORCO | +2.19 | +0.314 | +0.192 | +0.972 | +0.342 | | Or19a + ORCO | +9.43 | +0.051 | +0.067 | +0.157 | +0.028 | | Or22a + ORCO | +15.10 | +0.140 | +0.049 | +0.151 | +0.092 | | Or35a + ORCO | +38.06 | +0.020 | +0.038 | +0.084 | +0.012 | | Or42a + ORCO | +39.54 | -0.010 | -0.016 | +0.214 | -0.001 | | Or59b + ORCO | +18.71 | +0.034 | +0.032 | +0.201 | +0.141 | | Or67a + ORCO | +22.50 | -0.030 | +0.040 | +0.036 | +0.042 | | Or67b + ORCO | +14.20 | -0.031 | +0.010 | +0.003 | -0.015 | | Or85b + ORCO | +18.99 | +0.019 | +0.056 | +0.093 | +0.027 | | Or98a + ORCO | +30.83 | +0.012 | +0.020 | +0.103 | +0.033 | | ORCO only | +19.61 | -0.058 | +0.017 | +0.018 | +0.013 | The reference magnitude matters. Or7a has the smallest VUAA1-minus-DMSO reference (**+2.19 pp**); its valeric-acid contrast is **+2.13 pp**, producing **N = 0.972**. This ratio does not establish a stronger absolute response than Or42a, whose valeric-acid contrast is **+8.47 pp** and N is **0.214**. Or7a's VUAA1 F1 trajectory decreases; its positive S comes from a smaller decline than F0. A positive reference difference is therefore not proof of strong VUAA1 activation. [Zboray et al. (2023)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10709440/) normalized VOC responses by the same-day mean VUAA1 response of the corresponding stable cell line. That supplies a methodological precedent for reference scaling. Our added DMSO anchor, transient expression, single wells and different endpoint statistic make this an exploratory adaptation. VUAA1 is not a measured transfection fraction or an established maximum response in this dataset. The ratio expresses an odorant contrast relative to the construct's VUAA1 reference; it cannot isolate expression level, correct each odorant well's transfection efficiency, establish receptor specificity or provide a concentration-response curve. The ratio is shown only for Test 2. Test 1 has a different response statistic, several nonpositive control-referenced VUAA1 denominators, and a buffer reference that is not a documented matched VUAA1 vehicle. It is not placed on the same normalized scale. No uncertainty intervals or reliability threshold are inferred from repeated time readings of these single wells. Attachments: [all 66 Test 2 ratios, including the two reference anchors](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/617cee2111a3-test2-vuaa1-referenced-summary.csv), [method and source metadata](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/4f4d86622302-vuaa1-normalization.json) and [normalization audit, including Test 1 exclusions](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/470612269af5-vuaa1-normalization-audit.csv).

entries.title: Or35a: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.text: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the Or35a+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 4**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Disturbance-corrected fluorescence profile ![Or35a: within-acquisition fluorescence changes and corrected endpoints](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/f713c4ba663254c55262e1d0563db68227cc4fb5ec2e55d32d0aa327dac815f4.avif) *Each acquisition is normalized to its own first reading. F0 covers 0–48 s; F1 covers 0–168 s, with separate stage labels. The endpoint contrast subtracts the observed F0 drift from the observed F1 change. No injection-aligned continuous trace, extrapolated baseline or biological replicate error bar is inferred.* ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A04 | VUAA1 | -2.57 | +34.09 | +36.67 | +38.06 | +19.67 | | D04 | Isopentyl acetate | -2.06 | -2.68 | -0.61 | +0.78 | +0.60 | | E04 | 2-Heptanone | -3.10 | -3.04 | +0.05 | +1.44 | +1.58 | | F04 | Valeric acid | -2.72 | -0.91 | +1.81 | +3.20 | +1.14 | | G04 | Pentyl acetate | -2.17 | -3.10 | -0.93 | +0.46 | +0.75 | | H04 | DMSO vehicle | -1.60 | -2.99 | -1.39 | +0.00 | -0.11 | ### Interpretation For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+34.09%**, while F0 changes **-2.57%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +36.67 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -1.39 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+38.06 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +19.67 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+38.06 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.
